B12_00: A thickened patch of epithelium invaginates, deepens into a cup and pinches off from the surface sheet to form a closed hollow vesicle. Fibroblast growth factor ligands acting through their receptor tyrosine kinase induce and shape the thickening, while transcription factors drive epithelial bending and assign regional identity. Ciliary and structural proteins support the cell-shape changes that allow the vesicle to close and separate.
B12_01: Cells choosing between alternative germ-layer fates are biased toward an endodermal programme by several modulating inputs. A secreted Wnt antagonist reshapes Wnt and nodal signalling gradients, a bHLH transcription factor helps define the boundary with the competing lineage, a histone variant marking facultative heterochromatin restricts which gene programmes stay accessible, and fibrillar collagen in the extracellular matrix supplies positional cues to migrating cells.
B12_02: A tissue is periodically segmented into repeating blocks by an oscillating gene-expression clock. Notch ligand-receptor signalling couples neighbouring cells, and a Fringe glycosyltransferase modifies the receptor to tune ligand sensitivity, keeping oscillations periodic and synchronised. Caudal-type homeobox transcription factors maintain the progenitor pool from which new segments are added, and a DM-domain transcription factor fixes polarity and competence within each newly formed segment.
B12_03: A population of progenitor cells is set aside and directed into a distinct developmental territory by combined BMP, non-canonical Wnt, canonical Wnt and Notch signalling. A LIM-homeodomain transcription factor maintains the undifferentiated progenitor state, while a MADS-box transcription factor and a SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling subunit activate the transcriptional programme that commits these cells to a contractile muscle fate.
B12_04: An epithelial tube forms a localized outgrowth that bulges out until a distinct bud exists. A secreted neurotrophic-family ligand from neighbouring mesenchyme induces the outgrowth through its receptor tyrosine kinase, with homeobox transcription factors controlling ligand production and a zinc-finger factor restricting where it is received. Heparan sulfate sulfation shapes ligand presentation, and BMP antagonists relieve BMP inhibition so budding occurs at a single site.
B12_05: Each newly forming segment is polarised into front and back halves before any physical boundary appears. Oscillatory clock and Notch signals converge to induce bHLH transcription factors in the anterior half, a T-box factor licenses their expression and a Notch-regulated ankyrin protein tunes Notch output. Ripply-family corepressors then feed back to extinguish T-box and bHLH activity, sharpening the boundary, while a FERM protein links polarity to epithelialisation.
B12_06: A solid cord of epithelial cells is hollowed out to create a continuous lumen, converting the cord into an open conduit. A TNF-family ligand and its receptor drive the process, Hedgehog signalling and an NFI-family transcription factor provide patterning and branching context, and transglutaminase crosslinking remodels the surrounding matrix. Lumen clearance proceeds through programmed cell death of central cells together with cell rearrangement.
B12_07: Signals that promote formation of epithelial and endothelial tubes act mainly through growth factors that stimulate cells to proliferate, migrate and organise into lumenised cords. Receptor activation is relayed by PI3K to cytoskeletal and survival responses. Homeobox and zinc-finger transcription factors specify responsive progenitors and sustain growth factor expression, while extracellular matrix proteins shape the environment that guides tube assembly.
B12_08: Golgi-derived vesicles are trafficked, tethered and fused into a single large secretory organelle that caps one pole of the nucleus. Rab GTPase-activating proteins, Golgi tethering factors and membrane fusion machinery deliver the vesicles, and an actin-based anchoring scaffold attaches the organelle to the nuclear envelope and couples it to nuclear shaping. Packaged cargo includes hydrolases and adhesion proteins used later in membrane binding and fusion.
B12_09: Glial cells extend processes that spiral around axons and compact their own plasma membrane into a multilayered insulating sheath. Adhesion molecules mediate recognition between glial membrane and axon surface, lipid synthesis and intracellular trafficking build a membrane of unusual lipid composition, and regulators of differentiation control process outgrowth. The process couples glial membrane biogenesis to axon-glia signalling, enabling fast saltatory conduction.
B12_10: Extracellular signals control how many cells adopt a mesodermal fate, and where and when. Wnt ligands drive the fate switch, while secreted antagonists that block Wnt receptors restrain the responding domain. BMP receptor signalling patterns subregions, and FGF receptor signalling is needed for cells to ingress and acquire mesodermal identity. A bHLH transcription factor then marks and specifies a subset of the newly formed mesoderm.
B12_11: A flat epithelial sheet bends into a groove as its edges thicken and elevate toward one another, preparing for later fusion into a tube. BMP and nodal ligands supply dorsoventral patterning cues, while cofilin-mediated actin severing and other cytoskeletal regulators drive apical constriction and cell-shape changes that create hinge points. Chromatin remodelling and transcriptional regulators couple these signals to gene expression.
B12_12: Cells become competent to differentiate as endoderm, though the commitment remains reversible. Starting from a pluripotent transcriptional state, a SoxB factor is switched off as an endoderm-specific Sox factor is switched on, and a T-box factor cooperates with nodal signalling to favour endoderm over mesoderm. A homeodomain factor carries the decision forward, and a secreted Wnt antagonist biases regional identity.
B12_13: Nascent actin bundles are organised into mature, aligned myofibrils with repeating sarcomeres. Actin and myosin light chains form the contractile core, a giant elastic protein acts as a molecular ruler spanning each sarcomere, and Z-disc proteins anchor it and couple mechanical strain to signalling. Formins and nebulin-related proteins organise and set thin filament length, and a light chain kinase tunes contractility.
B12_14: An epithelial tube is separated from a common foregut-like precursor and patterned along its dorsoventral axis through epithelial-mesenchymal crosstalk. BMP and TGF-beta ligands from the surrounding mesenchyme, canonical Wnt signalling through beta-catenin in the epithelium, and the MEK-ERK kinase cascade relay growth factor input into proliferation and patterning, deciding where a new identity begins and where cartilage and smooth muscle differentiate.
B12_15: Each newly formed segment acquires its own positional identity and is subdivided into compartments. Notch ligand signalling supplies the oscillatory and boundary-forming cue, a Ripply-family corepressor terminates that cue and sharpens the anterior-posterior subdivision within each segment, and homeobox transcription factors specify the distinct sub-compartment fates. The process converts transient periodic patterning into stable segmental identity.
B12_16: Actin thin filaments are assembled to a defined length and anchored within each sarcomere. Alpha-actin polymerises into the filament core, a leiomodin nucleates new filaments and caps them to set length, a giant elastic protein spans the sarcomere as a ruler, and a Z-disc protein binds its end to anchor the lattice. Transcriptional regulators establish the sarcomeric gene programme that supports filament sliding.
B12_17: One cell population signals to a neighbouring one and redirects its fate, typically through reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. Fibroblast growth factors with their receptors and adaptors, BMPs and Wnt ligands acting through beta-catenin carry the signals, while Dickkopf and Sprouty proteins restrain Wnt and FGF output to keep induction spatially bounded. Transcription factors read these cues and fix regional identity, and a neurotrophic-factor ligand initiates branching.
B12_18: Epithelial buds emerge from an epithelium and grow outward under reciprocal epithelial-mesenchymal signalling. Nuclear androgen receptor signalling in the mesenchyme licenses budding, epithelial Hedgehog and mesenchymal non-canonical Wnt position and restrain outgrowth, and BMP ligands act as inhibitors that limit bud number. An extracellular heparan sulfate 6-O-endosulfatase tunes the availability of matrix-bound growth factors, setting bud number and branching architecture.
B12_19: Mesenchymal cells epithelialise into a patent duct that extends in one direction and inserts into a target epithelium. Paired-box and zinc-finger transcription factors specify and maintain the duct epithelium and guide its extension, a homeodomain factor shapes tubular epithelial identity, and BMP and Wnt ligands from surrounding cells provide instructive signals, with the Wnt ligand later inducing neighbouring mesenchyme.
B12_20: A posterior progenitor zone grows and extends the body axis so that new segments can be laid down progressively behind it. Canonical Wnt ligand maintains the progenitors, a secreted frizzled-related protein sequesters Wnt and a Naked-family protein acts as induced negative feedback, tuning pathway output. A Mediator subunit links the pathway to transcription, and a PP2A regulatory subunit provides phosphorylation-dependent control.
B12_21: Mesenchymal cells undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition and organise into an epithelial tube. Paired-box transcription factors act partly redundantly to specify and maintain the epithelial state, Sox factors contribute to progenitor behaviour, and a Wnt ligand from neighbouring epithelium induces a second Wnt ligand in the mesenchyme that drives the transition. Inductive Wnt signalling is thereby linked to lineage specification and tube morphogenesis.
B12_22: The proliferative window of committed but still dividing precursor cells is controlled to set how many cells are produced before differentiation. A LIM-homeodomain factor maintains the undifferentiated state, a Six-Eya transcriptional complex and a Notch-effector bHLH repressor restrain or sustain division, bHLH and T-box factors pattern the lineage, and beta-catenin couples Wnt input to precursor expansion, linking fate commitment to cell cycle control.
B12_23: Edges of an epithelial fold bend, meet and fuse to seal a tube with a central lumen. Planar cell polarity components drive convergent extension, actin regulators constrict apical surfaces, and Hedgehog, BMP and Wnt signalling, with secreted antagonists, pattern the epithelium. Folate one-carbon metabolism supports proliferation, cilia and intraflagellar transport tune signalling, and caspase-mediated apoptosis remodels the fusing seam.
B12_24: Cells emerging from a progenitor region are allocated to one mesodermal fate and moved collectively into position. Wnt ligands acting through canonical and non-canonical routes drive both fate allocation and coordinated migration, with an LEF/TCF factor transducing canonical signals to target genes. Forkhead transcription factors act redundantly to maintain this identity, and exocyst-mediated vesicle trafficking delivers membrane for polarized migration and convergent extension.
B12_25: Upstream signals promote and accelerate assembly of actin and myosin into sarcomeres bounded by Z discs. A BMP-family growth factor and a vasoactive peptide act as paracrine cues, a myosin light chain kinase and a protein kinase C-related kinase phosphorylate targets that control filament assembly and Z-disc gene expression, a transcription factor contributes patterning input, and a microRNA tunes output.
B12_26: A septate-like junction is assembled where the edges of a myelin sheath contact the axon, sealing the sheath to the axonal membrane. An axonal neurexin-family adhesion protein partners with contactin to bind glial neurofascin, a band 4.1-like protein links the complex to the cytoskeleton, and a tetraspanin organizes the membrane. Galactolipid and ether lipid synthesis supply lipids needed for junction integrity, which segregates ion channel domains.
